ui_bugs.issue: The Tags filter row shows LAST-SEEN casing instead of FIRST-SPELLING-WINS. In /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/history.tsx line 273-277, the Map keyed by lowercase overwrites earlier entries, so if any scan happens to carry a legacy lowercase 'big 8' tag, the filter row chip renders as 'big 8' even though two other scans tagged it as 'Big 8'. Observed: Tags row rendered 'big 8' | 'Creek Stand' (lowercase big 8). Not functionality-breaking (case-insensitive match still works), but inconsistent with backend tag endpoint which keeps first-spelling-wins. Fix: iterate scans in order and only setDefault into the Map (if (!map.has(key)) map.set(key, tag.trim())), OR sort scans by created_at desc and reduce.

Non-fatal but should be hunted down - likely a stray whitespace between <View> children in dateSeasonRow or tagsRow in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/history.tsx.

rca_of_issue: The one minor bug (filter-row chip shows lowercase when a legacy lowercase scan is present): /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/history.tsx builds allTags via `new Map(flatMap(scan.tags).map(t=>[t.toLowerCase(),t.trim()])).values()`. The Map's constructor overwrites on duplicate keys with the LAST pair, so a later lowercase 'big 8' overwrites an earlier 'Big 8'. Backend's dedup is first-spelling-wins (reversed trick). The two layers are inconsistent. Fix: `const map = new Map(); scans.flatMap(s=>s.tags||[]).forEach(t=>{const k=t.trim().toLowerCase(); if(!map.has(k)) map.set(k, t.trim());}); const allTags = [...map.values()].filter(Boolean).sort((a,b)=>a.localeCompare(b));`
